draft.title: Resistance and Ohm's law
card: Resistance is how much a component opposes current. It is measured in ohms (Ω). A higher resistance means less current for the same voltage.
Ohm's law links the three quantities: V = IR. Voltage V is in volts, current I is in amperes and resistance R is in ohms.
a device whose resistance stays constant as the voltage changes. Its graph of current against voltage is a straight line through the origin.
a device whose resistance changes as the voltage changes, such as a diode. Its current against voltage graph is not a straight line.
draft.remember: V = IR. In an ohmic device, R stays constant, so current is proportional to voltage.

a.q: A resistor has 12 V across it and a current of 3.0 A through it. What is its resistance?
a.why: Rearranging V = IR gives R = V ÷ I = 12 ÷ 3.0 = 4.0 Ω. Multiplying the two numbers to get 36 Ω would find V × I, which is not the resistance.
a.clue: Rearrange V = IR to make R the subject.

b.q: A student raises the voltage across a component and finds that the current rises, but the current against voltage graph curves and is not a straight line. What can be concluded?
opts: Its resistance changes, so it is non-ohmic
Its resistance is constant, so it is ohmic
Its resistance is zero, so it is ohmic
Its current is constant, so it is non-ohmic
b.why: A curved graph means the ratio V ÷ I is not constant, so the resistance changes and the device is non-ohmic. The fact that current rises with voltage does not make it ohmic, because an ohmic device needs a straight line through the origin.
b.clue: What shape of graph does a constant resistance give?

b.best: Its resistance changes, so it is non-ohmic
